assignments.rationale: The repository's primary product is a benchmark suite and evaluation harness for vision-language models: it ships a vendored lmms-eval fork with 20 registered model wrappers (5 more commented out) (local vLLM, local Hugging Face, and API providers), 72 per-model launcher scripts across the three task families, per-task YAML definitions with metric aggregation hooks, a parse-and-summarize stage that computes reproducible SuccessRate / MAE / MRE / nMAE / IoU / F1 metrics, an LLM-as-judge second-pass parser, and a published leaderboard. This matches the family scope of model-centric benchmark suites, evaluation harnesses, datasets, and reproducible metrics for language and vision-language models.

evidence.description: The Benchmark section defines the evaluation protocol: per-subtask sample limits, the three subtask rosters, and the four pipeline steps (evaluate, parse, summarize, LLM-judge re-parse).
AVAILABLE_MODELS registry of the vendored evaluation harness, mapping each supported vision-language model key to its wrapper class.
The benchmark's answer-extraction and per-sample scoring stage that turns raw model outputs into the published metric records.
Package metadata declaring medvision_bm as the codebase for the MedVision benchmark, with the mvbm console entry point.
A representative per-model evaluation launcher showing the harness invocation, sample limit, token budget, and result-tree conventions.

assignments.rationale: Detection is one of the three first-class tasks and the largest by far: models must localize anatomical structures, tumors and lesions on 2D medical slices as bounding boxes, scored with region-based IoU, F1, Precision and Recall plus box-to-image-ratio stratified analyses. The repository owns the detection ground-truth conventions (boxes fitted per mask cluster, single-instance filtering), a dedicated detection summarizer, detection-specific analysis tools, and a 110K-sample detection training set used to post-train the released model. This is localization and detection of lesions, abnormalities and anatomical structures in medical images, not a generic object-detection library.

evidence.description: Region-based detection metric implementations (cal_IoU, cal_F1, cal_Precision, cal_Recall, cal_metrics_detection_task) operating on medical-image bounding boxes.
The detection-task summarizer that aggregates per-sample box metrics by anatomy, imaging modality and slice plane.
Detection analysis stratified by box-to-image ratio, quantifying performance on small, medium and large anatomical targets.
The detection benchmark roster listing the per-dataset detection subtasks over anatomical and lesion targets.

assignments.rationale: The repository contains a first-class supervised fine-tuning stack for vision-language models, not merely a training example: ten trainer entry points covering four model families (eight CoT LoRA/full-FT, one non-CoT, one tool-use), both LoRA/parameter-efficient and full-parameter FSDP paths, per-family collate and loss-masking utilities, multi-task dataset construction with sample-limit and validation-split semantics, a temperature-scaled multi-task sampler, and checkpoint merging and publishing. It was used to produce the released MedVision-V0 model and has its own documented section in the project README.

evidence.description: The supervised fine-tuning core: prepare_trainer builds the parameter-efficient LoRA trainer and prepare_trainer_fullFT builds the full-parameter FSDP trainer.
A LoRA chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning entry point for a vision-language model family.
The corresponding full-parameter fine-tuning entry point, showing that full SFT is a supported path rather than an example.
The Training: SFT section documenting the fine-tuning launchers, their configuration variables, and the resource-constrained settings.
